It's happening! I was hoping Relic has kept busy since their Sega acquisition. Dawn of War III Announcement Trailer

As much as I am happy to see a new DoW title, there's some red lights in the trailer (and this PC Gamer article http://archive.is/b3QEN) for me

  1. Only 3 armies - which probably means DLC up the arse, especially with the unholy union of Sega (Total Faction DLC) and GW (Let's double all prices again!)
  2. Constant talk about "accessibility", which could mean anything from visual changes to merrily dumbing down the game
  3. And this:

For multiplayer, inspired by Dota's hero selection phase, Relic designers are considering an element of pick and counter-pick to the pre-battle screen, though they're yet to show exactly how this will work.

Many fans already complained that DoW 2 already felt like too much of a Dota clone, so while it's nice that base-building is back, I'd rather not have the game mutate into another party of "Whack-the-hero".

I'd actually be OK with army DLC. Back in the day I paid $50 for Space Marines, Chaos Marines, Eldar and Orks, then another $20 for Imperial Guard, then another $40 for Dark Eldar and Necron, then another $20 for Sisters of Battle. And I probably got wrong which expansion added which race. The Tau went in there at some point.

Bottom line is that after 3 expansions Dawn of War had 5 more races. Granted we also got full single player campaigns with those.

I'm willing to go wait and see with the rest. I'm mostly a single player guy anyways.

I'd argue that the single player campaigns coupled with two new races (plus one new unit for all old races) in DC and SS actually made them worth their money (Winter Assault always was debatable regarding anything other than Sturnn being the manliest motherfucker in the galaxy).

What I fear is that you'll see $10 DLCs for individual factions such as Dark Eldar or Necrons with no further content but the bareboned units attached. And then four different faction DLCs for Chaos so you can play cult legions, special faction DLCs for Space Yiffs/Blood Angels/Dark Angels, and so forth.

You may end up being correct. But with any luck, we'll see a Season Pass/Game of the Year edition which sums up all the most worthy DLC. It'll just require some patience. Which isn't the optimal solution, granted.
